Hi Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited to test Redwood for recommendation features across three different product teams. Before we move forward I have a few billing questions from procurement so we don’t delay legal/vendor setup: 

- Does Redwood support a monthly invoicing cadence billed on Net45 terms? Our standard is Net45 and procurement will expect that on a PO.
- Can you consolidate usage across multiple projects under a single vendor account / single monthly invoice (we have three internal billing codes)?
- What information do you need from our side to enable Net45 (credit app, references, initial PO, ACH details)?
- Is card-on-file required as fallback or is invoice-only allowed for approved customers?

Also: is there any discounting or pricing floor for invoiced customers vs card customers? We’re trying to estimate monthly spend and how that affects approval timelines. Procurement will likely attach a PO if Net45 is possible. I’ve attached our internal PO template to speed things up.

Thanks — Samantha

Samantha — appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, then next steps: 

- Net45: Yes, we can support Net45 on a case-by-case basis. It requires a brief credit review and an approved PO on file. For new enterprise accounts we typically attach a short SOW describing billing cadence and billing entity.
- Consolidated invoice: Also supported — we can roll multiple projects/teams into one monthly invoice and optionally include line-level billing codes you provide.
- Card fallback: Card-on-file is not strictly required if Net45 is approved; however, we typically keep a payment method on file as a backup for billing failures unless a prepayment/commit is arranged.
- Discounting: We do offer invoice-only pricing adjustments for committed volume. For Net45 requests we review requested commit and term before granting discounts.

What we need from Acme to set this up:
1) Signed PO referencing our vendor name (Redwood Inference, Inc.), payment terms (Net45), and billing address.
2) Billing contact email for invoice delivery (we can send to procurement@acmeretail.com and cc team-level contacts).
3) Expected monthly spend (or a commit) so we can confirm pricing and any discount.
4) If you require ACH setup, our finance team will send bank details and a W-9.

I’ve looped in Ben (sales) for discount path and Laura (finance) for the credit setup and SOW. Attached a short SOW template that lists Net45 as the payment term so procurement can attach it to the PO.

If that works, can you confirm the billing contact and an estimated monthly usage this quarter? Once we have the PO, Laura will kick off the short credit review and we’ll aim to get Net45 enabled for the following billing cycle.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Samantha — quick note from the commercial side. We can approve Net45 + consolidated invoicing for Acme pending:

- A 6-month minimum commit (forecasted monthly usage) OR an explicit PO for the first 2 months as bridge while credit completes.
- Standard 7% invoice-only discount for that commit band (we can adjust based on usage).

If you’re able to share a high-level monthly token/embedding estimate, I’ll run the math and include the discount in the formal quote. If Acme prefers no commit, we can still enable Net45 but would require a payment method on file and a shorter evaluation period (Net30).
